2.3.8 Summary 
Cognitive load theory underscores the need to optimise the quantity of 
information, presented and processed by students, to enhance their knowledge 
retention and understanding. Self-regulatory and self-determined learning are 
critical factors for motivation and academic performance; however, their usage 
should be managed to limit extraneous load. With additional utilisation of spaced 
repetition, students are more likely to remember information over longer 
durations, reducing cognitive load and the need for cramming. 
Microlearning places itself as a potential solution to reduced attention spans, 
offering improved engagement, motivation and learning outcomes. Assessments 
when designed to provoke deeper thought and personal analytics, emerge as 
essential components to the aid the learning experience. The literature suggests 
when cognitive load is managed, content is brief and highly informative, active 
learning is utilised, and assessments provoke deeper thoughts; a learning 
environment will be created that will maximise the chances of a student 
achieving their academic goals. 
2.4 Technologies in e-Learning 
2.4.1 Interactive Simulation Games and Virtual Laboratories

all components and can be accessed remotely.
